repository_acquisition.objective: Follow open-kernel-driver-port/references/acquisition.md for version selection. Choose exactly one source, target and QEMU upstream repository/ref for the frozen envelope, inspecting supplied_upstream_baselines and metadata only. Do not clone, fetch, resolve tags or write provenance; the controller performs acquisition, revision resolution and identity recording. Return the selection through the controller protocol.

evidence_closure.objective: Follow open-kernel-driver-port/references/acquisition.md and handoff.md to choose the task-relevant evidence facets. This stage owns the material selection, rationale, source/provenance requirements and explicit gaps; the controller acquires content and records hashes and provenance. Do not use this stage for compiler/layout probes, C semantic closure, target API study, migration contracts, implementation or QEMU execution. Submit selections through the controller protocol and preserve valid selections on repair.

environment_recovery.objective: Follow open-kernel-driver-port/references/environment-recovery.md using frozen repositories and inventory.local_probes. This stage owns the artifact mode, executable experiment route and environment entrypoint; it does not perform target API study, source-contract design or driver implementation. Submit the environment report and entrypoint through the controller protocol.

target_platform_study.objective: Complete knowledge-guided-driver-port/references/target-platform-study.md, including its referenced profile, using the supplied originals and project KB Skill. This stage owns target API definitions and call sites, the analogous target path, initialization/ownership/context facts, packaging route evidence and the necessity of any target change. Explicitly record every driver prerequisite whose target interface is absent or incomplete in a capability-gap register, linking each gap to direct target evidence, affected contract area, alternatives considered and the exact enablement work required; do not implement the change in this stage. It does not implement Rust, close the C translation contracts or test provenance, prepare the final runtime artifact, or run the public QEMU ladder. Optional aid for Linux-to-Asterinas tasks: if useful and available, you may consult linux-asterinas-driver-map/SKILL.md under instructions.skill_root, selecting Asterinas pages for relevant bus/device/mechanism questions. These are guides to the original kernels, not evidence of the current migration implementation. Reading or recording use of this optional guide is not required for stage acceptance; rely on this run's frozen originals for conclusions. Do not load the whole collection.

migration_contracts.objective: Complete knowledge-guided-driver-port/references/workflow.md phases 3–5, following translation.md, knowledge-contract.md and test-porting.md. This stage owns source closure, bounded compiler/preprocessor/layout/effect evidence, migration contracts and test stimulus/assertion provenance; use the accepted target study as an input. It does not implement Rust, change the target tree, prepare the runtime artifact or run public QEMU. Submit source analysis, contracts and test selection in the stage report. Do not end with DPF_SELF_REVIEW: PASS while a required compiler/configuration/layout/effect fact, translation contract, or test assertion provenance is explicitly left as a future gate; complete the bounded check or report a concrete blocker. Optional aid for Linux-to-Asterinas tasks: if useful and available, you may consult linux-asterinas-driver-map/SKILL.md under instructions.skill_root, selecting Linux pages for source paths and comparison pages for migration mappings. These are guides to the original kernels, not evidence of the current migration implementation. Reading or recording use of this optional guide is not required for stage acceptance; rely on this run's frozen originals for conclusions. Do not load the whole collection.

target_framework_enablement.objective: Complete the target-framework enablement stage described by target-framework-enablement.md. Consume the frozen target study and migration contracts, implement only the minimal evidenced target API/framework capabilities they require, validate the target change and affected regressions, and submit a report. Do not edit the migrated driver, runtime artifact, QEMU harness or unrelated target code; do not introduce a fallback or dual path.

driver_implementation.objective: Complete knowledge-guided-driver-port/references/workflow.md phases 6–7, following translation.md, target-changes.md and test-porting.md. Use the existing target study and migration contracts as frozen design inputs. This stage owns the Rust driver, necessary target changes, public tests, compliance self-check and implementation snapshot. Before submission, build the current implementation and run a bounded target functional smoke under qemu-evidence.md: component initialization, exact device identity, registration, probe/binding/readiness and one applicable data operation, including externally observed TX/RX for network drivers. Prepare implementation-smoke.sh, runtime-artifact and check-presence.sh under .dpf-output for controller execution. Diagnose and repair smoke failures locally until passing; use prerequisite repair only for an evidenced earlier defect. Do not silently revise scope, target study, contracts or test provenance. Artifact preparation reuses the resulting image when valid; the full public QEMU ladder remains in public_qemu_validation.

artifact_preparation.objective: Prepare and identify the runtime artifact under knowledge-guided-driver-port/references/qemu-evidence.md. Use the existing implementation, contracts and test plan. This stage owns packaging/injection, the presence checker and artifact identity; keep source changes limited to necessary packaging or integration wiring and route behavioral changes back to driver_implementation. Do not perform the public QEMU evidence ladder here. Submit through the controller protocol.

public_qemu_validation.objective: Consume the artifact and identity fixed by artifact_preparation and complete knowledge-guided-driver-port/references/workflow.md phase 8's public QEMU evidence ladder plus phase 9's narrow failure attribution under qemu-evidence.md. This stage owns the public runner, harness/oracles and interpretation of controller receipts; it does not rebuild or redesign the driver artifact on the normal path. Update the same report with each required result, attribution and limit, then complete the worker self-check. The independent final evidence audit is final_evidence_review, not a second artifact-preparation task.

final_evidence_review.objective: Independently perform knowledge-guided-driver-port/references/workflow.md phase 11 (Final evidence audit) over the current implementation, target changes, runtime artifact and public QEMU evidence. Treat the supplied contract and test-matrix digests as frozen acceptance oracles; do not re-review target study, handoff, source closure or contract provenance. Apply the final-evidence-review rules, cite precise code and authoritative execution evidence, and return all delivery findings together. Treat human-readable artifact receipts and worker summaries as derived metadata; a receipt-only mismatch is not a packaging defect and must not trigger artifact preparation or a new QEMU run. Accept only complete agreed functionality, otherwise request the smallest evidenced repair or report a genuine external blocker.

analysis_review.objective: Independently review the completed target-platform study, source analysis, migration contracts and test plan before implementation and before sealing the evidence/design phase. Apply the shared review rules. Verify key evidence locations and whether originals actually support core behavior, API availability/blocker claims and existing test coverage. Use the read-only Python locator explicitly for source references. Check the intended target architecture/artifact route separately from any standalone QEMU model smoke. Review all assigned materials, then return all findings together with precise report/source line references and reasons. Judge readiness for implementation; planned implementation and runtime tests are not missing analysis deliverables. Request the earliest affected permitted prerequisite for substantive defects; use BLOCKED only for a genuine external prerequisite or sealed premise.
